attributes.body_ja:
「わけがない」は、名詞（めいし）の「わけ」を使（つか）った、強（つよ）い否定（ひてい）の表現（ひょうげん）です。「絶対（ぜったい）に (A) ではない」や「(A) は不可能（ふかのう）だ」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。この文法（ぶんぽう）は、「わけ」と、助詞（じょし）「が」、形容詞（けいようし）「ない」からできています。

「わけがない」は、連体形（れんたいけい）の動詞（どうし）や形容詞（けいようし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「わけがない」は、「わけではない」より強（つよ）い表現（ひょうげん）です。「わけではない」は、「(A) の可能性（かのうせい）はあるけど、そうではない」のような部分的（ぶぶんてき）な否定（ひてい）を表（あらわ）しますが、「わけがない」は「(A) であることは１００（ひゃく）％（パーセント）ない」という完全（かんぜん）な否定（ひてい）を表（あらわ）します。
attributes.body:
One of the strongest ways to use the noun わけ in Japanese, is in the expression わけがない. This is regularly translated as 'there is no way that (A)', or 'it is impossible that (A)'. However, as mentioned in other わけ lessons, わけ is used very similarly to 'so' in English, so may also be thought of as 'it is SO not (A)', with 'so' being used for emphasis. In this structure, わけ is combined with the case marking particle が, and the い-Adjective ない.

わけがない may be used with verbs, or adjectives in their attributive form.

Caution

Compared to わけではない, わけがない is much stronger, and emphasizes the 'non-existence' of something. This can be thought of as similar to the difference between 'it is so that it isn't (A)' (for わけではない), and 'it is SO not (A)' (for わけがない).

'It is so that it isn't (A)' highlights that (A) is a thing that exists, but not in the way of (A). On the other hand, 'it is SO not (A)' highlights that no part of (A) whatsoever can be considered to be correct/accurate.

attributes.body: わけがない and ようがない・ようもない are similar in that both express impossibility. わけがない rejects something as logically unthinkable, e.g. 彼がそんなことをするわけがない ('There's no way he'd do that'). ようがない emphasizes that there is no way or means to do something, e.g. 助けようがない ('There's no way to help').

attributes.body: そうもない and わけがない are similar in that both express the unlikelihood of an event. そうもない suggests low probability based on observation, e.g. 雨が降りそうもない ('It seems unlikely that it'll rain'), while わけがない is an emphatic denial based on the speaker's logical conclusion, e.g. 勝てるわけがない ('There's no way we can win').

attributes.body: These expressions are similar in that both emphatically express negation, but they differ in nuance. ことはない implies something never happens, or literally 'there are no cases of (A)', e.g. 二度と会うことはない ('I'll never talk to him again / a second time.'). In contrast, わけがない expresses strong denial or impossibility, e.g. 負けるわけがない ('There's no way I can lose.')

attributes.body: Both of these patterns with わけ express negation, but with different nuances. わけではない denies a possible interpretation or assumption, e.g. 'it's not the case that (A)', while わけがない is a stronger, categorical denial, meaning 'there's no way that (A)' or '(A) is impossible'.

attributes.body: はずがない and わけがない are similar in that they both express a strong denial of a possibility, similar to the English 'There's no way that (A)', but with slightly different nuances. はずがない gives the sense that the speaker is drawing a conclusion based on their own reasoning, often with a sense of surprise or disbelief. In contrast, わけがない expresses an even stronger denial, as if the impossibility is an obvious fact.
